newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - DBS rates CITIC a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - DBS rates CITIC a buy.

text.p: DBS Securities said on Wednesday it had raised its rating on CITIC Pacific Ltd to buy from accumulate and said the stock could reach HK$52 over the next 12-months.

Research manager Philip Tulk said in a report that CITIC's purchase of a 20 percent stake in China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) should provide CITIC with good cashflow from dividends and an earnings boost from CLP's property portfolio.
"Potential for synergies in Hong Kong and China make this union an interesting one," he said.

The report said CITIC had an interest in participating in the management of the Hong Kong utility - not just helping CLP with its new China connections, but also in procuring, designing and managing new projects in China.
DBS said CITIC may increase its stake in CLP in the long run. It could inject its China power projects into CLP in return for new CLP shares.

A recent management acquisition of 330 million CITIC shares from parent CITIC Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd at HK$33 per share had been viewed negatively but DBS said it was positive for shareholders. "This will certainly align the interests of CITIC management with those of shareholders," it said.
The HK$33 per share price which management paid for the acquisition, which represented a discount of 27 percent to the previous day's close, caused a slide in CITIC's share price.
But DBS said CITIC Hong Kong could have been giving management a reward for their contribution to adding value to the share in the past.

By selling CITIC Pacific shares, CITIC Hong Kong could raise the cash to acquire assets and inject them back into CITIC Pacific, Tulk suggested. "It sells some shares, reaps some cash, invests in telecoms, injects the assets back into CITIC Pacific and takes more shares," the report said.
Several positive corporate events are also expected over the next year, "spin-offs of civil infrastructure and Dragonair, and a HK Telecom sale," Tulk predicted.
He said a spin-off of CITIC's civil infrastructure businesses - Hong Kong and China roads, bridges, tunnels and water projects - was a possibility in the near term.
He estimates at HK$8.2 billion CITIC's investments in China civil infrastructure, together with its interests in Hong Kong's Eastern Harbour Crossing and Western Harbour Crossing.
"The most likely scenario would be to spin-off 25 percent of such assets. On our estimates, this could result in an exceptional profit to CITIC of HK$1.4 billion," the report said.
DBS also said a sale of CITIC's eight percent Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd stake was inevitable.
At current prices, the stake is valued at HK$11.6 billion and CITIC would be able to book HK$4.4 billion exceptional profit on the sale, DBS said.

The long-awaited listing of Dragonair now looks to happen in early 1998, it added. A listing of 25 percent of Dragonair - the most likely scenario - would bring an exceptional gain of HK$472 million to CITIC, the report said.

As of Wednesday's close, CITIC shares were down 15.81 percent since the beginning of the year. The stock closed at HK$37.80 and DBS said it should trade at a premium of between 25 to 30 percent of net asset value which it values at HK$32.07.
It forecast 1996 net profit of HK$6.9 billion, up 124 percent year on year, and 1997 net profit of HK$4.23 billion.

"1998 should be a bell-weather year. We look for 48 percent growth in net earnings on the strength of a full year's contribution from CLP, property bookings..., the advent of the group's two new investment properties (the CITIC Building at Tamar and Festival Walk with Swire), and a good year at Cathay Pacific and Dragonair."
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
